text:
The banner outside Little Caesars Arena tells the story. Emmitt Finnie's face now hangs where Dylan Larkin's used to, as Sean Shapiro of EP Rinkside noted, and on the ice the 21-year-old stepped into a much bigger job during Larkin's long standoff, which ended with his trade to Montreal on Nov. 22. Finnie is skating 18:25 a night, up from 15:30 as a rookie, and his 15 points in 24 games are a breakout by our measure.

This is a 7th-round pick, 201st overall in 2023. The ten goals are a little ahead of his chances (7.6 expected), and a 20% shooting rate will cool. But the process is strong: Detroit gets 56.6% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, more than ten points better than without him. NHL EDGE has his speed bursts in the 99th percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he's a prime target for passes across the slot.

He just had a two-goal, three-point night against Vancouver. Watch whether the minutes hold now that Detroit has reshuffled its centers after the trade.
